name: beam-sharp
_comment: Derived from compiler/src/bs_lexer.xrl, which is the source of truth.
Pattern ORDER is significant: the first entry that matches at a position
wins, so the atom rule must precede the ':' operator and the comment rule
must precede everything (a '//' line may contain any token at all).

patterns._comment: A quoted atom, for what the bare sigil cannot spell. A record's minted tag is the case in point: :'Shop.Order'. Must precede the bare rule.
patterns.name: constant.other.symbol.quoted.beam-sharp

patterns._comment: The lexer's rule exactly: ':' then a lowercase start. Note there is NO space allowed, which is what makes `Id:int` colour ':int' as an atom while `Id: int` does not -- the same one-character trap the parser catches by name.
patterns.name: constant.other.symbol.beam-sharp

patterns._comment: `switch` is the only branching construct (ticket 17 §6); `when` introduces a guard on a clause or on a switch arm.
patterns.name: keyword.control.beam-sharp

patterns._comment: `raise` deliberately crashes and is the only spelling that produces one (ticket 12 §5). Scoped `exception` rather than sharing the line above, so a theme can colour the word that leaves without returning differently from the one that branches.
patterns.name: keyword.control.exception.beam-sharp

patterns._comment: `var` INTRODUCES a name (F8, ticket 45) and `where` carries a type's refinement predicate (F2, ticket 20 §5). `var` shipped with F8 and was never added here; the token gate says so by name, which is what it is for.
patterns.name: keyword.declaration.beam-sharp

patterns._comment: The one conjunction, in every position -- guard, pattern combinator and refinement predicate (ticket 44, amending ticket 08). There is no && and no ||.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.logical.beam-sharp

patterns._comment: The two keyword atoms. Bare, not sigilled -- and colouring them as constants rather than variables is the whole point: as identifiers they would be VARIABLES matching everything, which is the defect F7 found in the lexer.
patterns.name: constant.language.beam-sharp

parametric-builtin._comment: Only where a bracket follows. `list`, `option` and `result` are errors written without one (needs_type_args), so requiring the '<' is more accurate than a bare word list -- and it leaves `result` free to be an ordinary variable name, which it very plausibly is.
parametric-builtin.name: support.type.beam-sharp

field._comment: A PascalCase name before ':' is a field -- in a record declaration, in an anonymous map type, or in a property pattern. All three are `uident ':'` in the grammar.
field.name: variable.other.property.beam-sharp

function-name._comment: HEURISTIC, and the one place this grammar is guessing. A type and a function are the SAME token class (uident) -- only the compiler's symbol table can tell `Order` from `Describe`. A '(' after the name is the best a regex has. Semantic tokens over an LSP would fix this properly.
function-name.name: entity.name.function.beam-sharp

wildcard._comment: Exactly `_`. An identifier cannot START with an underscore in this language -- the lexer has no rule for one -- so `_foo` does not lex at all and is deliberately not matched here.
wildcard.name: variable.language.wildcard.beam-sharp

patterns._comment: Two arrows, two jobs: `->` is a clause, `=>` is a switch arm. Scoped apart so a theme can keep them apart.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.arrow.beam-sharp

patterns._comment: The pipe and the valve (ticket 17 §1 and §4, F14). BEFORE the catch-all below, which matches a bare `|` and would otherwise eat the first character of both.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.pipe.beam-sharp

patterns._comment: A binary pattern's opening bracket (ticket 30, F13). BEFORE the comparison rule, which would otherwise take `<` and leave a stray second one, and before the catch-all class at the bottom. There is deliberately NO `>>` rule here or in the lexer: `list<list<int>>` closes two generics, and the compiler's grammar closes a binary pattern on two separate `>` for exactly that reason.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.binary.beam-sharp

patterns._comment: `<` and `>` are BOTH a comparison and a generic bracket, and nothing in a regex can tell them apart -- see the README. Ticket 28 settled the rule positionally and F6.9 pins it.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.beam-sharp
